data.title: World's Top Battery Electrolyte Supplier Tinci to Invest up to USD749.5 Million in Capacity Expansion
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 13 -- Tinci Materials Technology, the world's largest supplier of lithium battery electrolytes, plans to invest up to CNY5 billion (USD749.5 million) to expand its production capacity for electrolytes and other key raw materials used in batteries.

The project, to be built near the company's existing plant in Chizhou, eastern Anhui province, will have an annual production capacity of 400,000 tons of lithium battery electrolyte and 100,000 tons of sodium battery electrolyte, the Guangzhou-based firm announced yesterday.

The new facilities will also produce various electrolyte chemicals, including liquid lithium hexafluorophosphate and sodium hexafluorophosphate, two key raw materials used in battery electrolytes.

Construction is expected to take 24 months. Once operational, the project will create an integrated production base for battery electrolytes and their chemical components in Chizhou, helping reduce transportation costs for raw materials and finished products and optimize the company's cost structure, Tinci said.

The investment will also strengthen the company's production capacity for core products and help ensure its ability to fulfill medium- and long-term orders, it said.

Tinci has been expanding sales to consolidate its leading position in the global market. The company sold more than 720,000 tons of lithium battery electrolyte last year, up about 44 percent from 2024, and held a global market share of 32.2 percent.

The company has also been securing major supply contracts. Last week, it reached an agreement with Chinese battery maker EVE Energy to supply a total of 450,000 tons of products over the next three years.

Meanwhile, Tinci is expanding its international presence. In addition to its factories in China, the company has begun supplying local customers through its original equipment manufacturing partners in the United States and Germany, according to its latest annual report. It is also building new factories in the US and Morocco.

Shares of Tinci [SHE: 002709] rose 2.5 percent in intraday trading today following the announcement, but reversed course to close down 2.2 percent as the Shenzhen Composite Index fell 2.1 percent.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: Drinda Sinks After Chinese Solar Cell Maker Scraps USD280 Million Oman Plant Plan
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 13 -- Shares in Hainan Drinda New Energy Technology plunged today after the Chinese supplier of N-type TOPCon photovoltaic cells said that it is abandoning plans to build a solar cell manufacturing base in Oman due to the evolving situation in the Middle East and growing uncertainty over tariff policies.

Drinda’s share price in Shenzhen [SHE: 002865] tumbled 8.8 percent to close at CNY12.23 (USD1.83). Its Hong Kong-traded stock [HKG: 2865] plummeted 10.4 percent to end the day at HKD12.05 (USD1.50).

Drinda is scrapping a plan, first announced in July 2024, to invest around USD280 million in a high-efficiency solar cell manufacturing facility with an annual production capacity of 5 gigawatts in Oman's Sohar Free Zone, the Haikou-based firm said yesterday. The project had been one of the company's key fundraising initiatives when it completed its secondary listing in Hong Kong in May last year.

Drinda cited several adverse factors behind the decision, including slower-than-expected progress, escalating international trade tensions and growing uncertainty over tariff policies in potential target markets.

In particular, the US-Iran conflict that broke out at the end of February this year has raised concerns over the stability of logistics routes, supply chain security and personnel safety in the region where the project is located, Drinda said.

In addition, China's Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Science and Technology announced plans in October to revise regulations and add certain photovoltaic technologies to the list of technologies subject to export prohibitions or restrictions. This has increased uncertainty over the regulatory and compliance requirements the project might face if it proceeded, Drinda added.

The company said the project had not entered the substantive implementation stage and therefore the decision to withdraw is not expected to have a material adverse impact on the firm’s existing operations.

Drinda raised net proceeds of HKD1.3 billion (USD164 million) from its secondary listing on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in May last year. According to its listing prospectus, HKD969 million of the proceeds had been earmarked for the Oman solar cell manufacturing project.

The firm said the funds originally allocated to the project would instead be used primarily for research and development of photovoltaic cell products, upgrades to existing production technologies and manufacturing lines, as well as raw material procurement and expansion into new application markets.

When Drinda first announced the Oman investment in 2024, it said the proposed facility would leverage the Sohar Free Zone's geographical advantages and trade policies to serve markets in the Middle East and Europe, while expanding its overseas production capacity and strengthening its international competitiveness.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: Nike Supplier Huali Eyes Stake in Data Center Supplier as Footwear Profits Tumble
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 13 -- Huali Industrial Group, a major Chinese manufacturer of athletic shoes for Nike, Adidas, and Converse, plans to invest up to USD500 million in an optical communications company as its core footwear business comes under pressure.

Huali is seeking to acquire a stake of no more than 25 percent in O-Net Technologies Group, a Cayman Islands-registered company undergoing restructuring to become a global holding platform for optical communications businesses, the Zhongshan-based firm recently announced. O-Net Technologies Shenzhen Group will serve as the platform's global operating headquarters and is separately preparing for an initial public offering on Shanghai's Star Market, the Nasdaq-style board for science and technology companies.

The footwear manufacturer said it plans to use idle funds to invest in optical communications, a field that uses light to transmit data at high speeds and is increasingly important for artificial intelligence data centers and telecommunications networks. Huali described the deal as a financial investment aimed at improving capital allocation and generating reasonable returns.

Huali also warned that investing outside its core industry carries risks, including insufficient knowledge of the optical communications sector and potential misjudgments about technological developments and market prospects.

The investment comes as Huali's core business faces shrinking sales and profits. Revenue fell 12 percent to CNY16.4 billion (USD2.5 billion) in the first nine months of this year, while net profit attributable to shareholders plunged 35 percent to CNY1.6 billion (USD236 million). Athletic shoe sales dropped 7 percent to 156 million pairs.

Growth among Huali's major customers has also slowed. Nike's revenue fell 4 percent year on year in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, including a 22 percent drop in China, while Converse's revenue slumped 28 percent. Hoka, which has been an important source of growth for Huali in recent years, reported single-digit revenue growth for two consecutive quarters.

Despite weakening demand, Huali has continued to expand production capacity. New factories in southwestern China's Sichuan province and Indonesia began operations last year, lifting the company's annual production capacity by 8 percent to 248 million pairs.

The expansion has proved challenging. In its interim report, Huali said new capacity had ramped up more slowly than expected, while increasingly frequent adjustments to production allocation and scheduling had reduced overall efficiency.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: China Takes Steps to Speed Up Third-Generation Nuclear Power Rollout
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 6 -- China is seeking to accelerate the introduction of its proprietary third-generation nuclear power technology by improving reactor design, digitizing project management, speeding up equipment production, and harmonizing technical standards. The push also involves bringing private investors into projects to widen the funding base and bolster the domestic supply chain.

China General Nuclear Power Group unveiled the Hualong One 2.0, a third-generation pressurized water reactor, in September, featuring improvements in safety, cost-effectiveness, and technological performance.

The upgraded reactor design is intended to boost the efficiency of both project management and construction by 20 percent, with the overall building period capped at 54 months, according to Kan Shuo, deputy director of the Project Management Engineering Technology Support Centre at China Nuclear Engineering Corporation.

At the end of last year, the generating capacity of nuclear power units in commercial operation in China was 62.5 million kilowatts, less than 2 percent of the nation’s total electricity production capacity. This leaves a significant gap to cover to reach the 200-million-kilowatt target projected by the China Nuclear Energy Association for 2040.

Addressing the pressure to meet delivery timelines, Kan noted that in February, China National Nuclear Corporation proposed integrating digital engineering concepts into the design-and-construction process. This allows for seamless flow of data across different project sectors, with the goal of achieving a 20 percent improvement in both management and construction efficiency, and capping the total project duration at 54 months.

The initial delivery estimate for a Hualong One 2.0 reactor was nearly 50 months, said Liu Chang, project management director at First Heavy Industries Dalian Nuclear Power & Petrochemical, a firm responsible for equipment manufacturing. But through process refinement, the delivery time is now expected to be just over 40 months, Liu noted.

Private Capital

In terms of capital, China has begun introducing private investment into nuclear power projects. The San'ao Nuclear Power Plant in Zhejiang province is the first to have private equity participation. The plant is set to have six 1,000-megawatt Hualong One units, with a total projected investment of CNY120 billion (USD17.9 billion).
 

Private investors have a 2 percent stake in the project's first phase, a figure that rises to 30 percent by the third phase, setting a record for the most private funding in China’s nuclear power sector. 

"The participation of private capital has become a key prerequisite for the approval of certain nuclear power projects,” said Xu Lingbin, deputy manager of general management at Cangnan Nuclear Power, which is responsible for building and running the San'ao Nuclear Power Plant.

“Private capital helps supplement the substantial equity funding required for these projects, and private enterprises with strong industrial backgrounds can foster synergy across the upstream and downstream supply chains," Xu told Yicai.

Unified Standards

Efforts are also underway to harmonize standards to facilitate faster project implementation. China’s two major nuclear power conglomerates, CGN and CNNC, previously used different technical standards. 

Efforts to harmonize standards began in 2017, but the alignment did not include a number of equipment components. As of 2024, atomic power industry regulators have pushed for further standardization, encompassing the entire project lifecycle, from design and construction to operation and decommissioning. 

"Promoting the unification of standards is a positive development for the manufacturing sector,” said Gao Dianbao, executive deputy general manager of First Heavy Industries Dalian Nuclear Power, which supplies equipment to both CGN and CNNC. “It streamlines processes and helps unlock production capacity," Gao added.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: Jaguar Land Rover Suffers Setback in BYD IP Dispute as Dutch Court Lifts Evidence Seizure Order
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 13 -- A Dutch court has overturned the evidence seizure order  Jaguar Land Rover had obtained against BYD and ordered the British carmaker to arrange for the destruction or return of the seized materials, marking a setback for Jaguar Land Rover in its ongoing intellectual property dispute with the Chinese auto manufacturer.

In its procedural ruling published on Nov. 11, the District Court of The Hague cited Article 705, paragraph 2 of the Dutch Code of Civil Procedure (Rv), and found that the seized materials were not necessary to establish whether BYD’s Ti7 infringed Jaguar Land Rover’s intellectual property rights.

The court also noted that both parties acknowledged that the Ti7 had not yet been sold in the European Union. Coventry-based Jaguar Land Rover had therefore failed to demonstrate that it had suffered market losses. The possibility of future infringement was not sufficient grounds for obtaining evidence at this stage.

On this basis, the court found that maintaining the seizure was unnecessary and that Jaguar Land Rover’s claim for damages appeared, on initial observation, unsubstantiated.

In August, Jaguar Land Rover alleged that BYD’s Ti7 infringed the EU design rights tied to its Defender model designation L663, and applied to a Dutch court for an order to preserve evidence.

On Aug. 24, bailiffs carried out the seizure at BYD's European headquarters and two Dutch offices in Schiedam and Hoofddorp. The materials taken reportedly included Ti7 launch plans, technical data, financial information and BYD's internal research records relating to the Defender, according to local media reports.

Under the ruling, Jaguar Land Rover must instruct the bailiff or judicial custodian to destroy the seized materials within 24 hours of formal service of the judgment. It must then provide Shenzhen-based BYD with confirmation of the materials' destruction within 24 hours of its completion. Failure to comply carries a penalty of EUR50,000 (USD55,300) per hour, capped at €500,000.

The court also rejected Jaguar Land Rover's separate claim for BYD to pay EUR500,000 (USD553,053) in contractual penalties.

This procedural ruling is not final. The judgment discloses that Jaguar Land Rover has separately filed preliminary-injunction proceedings. One is in The Hague concerning the Defender’s design rights, and another is in Rotterdam over its copyright and alleged "slavish imitation." Both cases are still pending.

Analysts say that intellectual-property disputes between Chinese automakers and established European carmakers are attracting increasing attention as Chinese brands accelerate their expansion into the European market.

The ruling shows that companies seeking to obtain competitors' internal business information through legal proceedings abroad must still meet local legal requirements on the necessity and relevance of the evidence.

Yicai has reached out to BYD for comment on the ruling and the ongoing legal proceedings, and as of publication had not received a response.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: BYD Raises Annual Overseas Sales Forecast 38% to 1.8 Mln Vehicles After Topping 1.5 Mln in 10 Months
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 10 -- Chinese new energy vehicle giant BYD has increased this year’s overseas sales forecast made at the beginning of the year by over 38 percent.

BYD expects to sell 1.8 million NEVs outside China in 2026, compared with the initial prediction of 1.3 million, Li Yunfei, general manager of BYD’s branding and public relations department, recently told the media, including Yicai. The firm sold just over 50,000 NEVs overseas in 2022.

Localized manufacturing and the construction of a global battery fast-charging network will create a deep moat for BYD overseas, Chairman Wang Chuanfu said on the 2025 earnings conference call, adding that the company aims for overseas markets to account for half of its total sales in the future.

BYD sold 3.62 million NEVs in the first 10 months of the year, of which 1.51 million were sold overseas, accounting for nearly 42 percent of the total, according to the firm’s latest production and sales data.

Beyond accelerating the roll-out of new models overseas, BYD is using premium models to open up the European and Middle Eastern markets and boost per-vehicle profit.

For example, BYD launched a new model under its Denza brand in the United Kingdom in July, priced from around CNY1.3 million (USD194,860), triple its price in China. Moreover, the firm recently unveiled its most expensive NEV model ever by presale price in the Middle East, estimated at around CNY2 million, with a deposit of CNY300,000 (USD44,970). Deliveries are slated for the second quarter of next year.

BYD’s management is confident of achieving the target of an average net profit per car sold overseas of about CNY20,000 (USD3,000) this year, according to a research report by Daiwa Securities. Regarding coping with overseas markets’ import tariffs, the management said the company’s plant in Brazil has already come online, and the one in Hungary will start production by the end of the year.

As for rising raw material and foreign exchange costs, BYD’s management noted that it will not raise prices on existing models but instead add more features, refresh model lineups, launch new models, and reprice its overall product portfolio.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: DeepSeek Harness Releases DAU Data for First Time, Topping 1.5 Million
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 6 -- Chinese artificial intelligence giant DeepSeek has released user data for DeepSeek Harness for the first time, revealing that the open-source agent harness framework has more than 1.5 million daily active users.

DeepSeek Harness had 1.54 million DAUs on its official application programming interface over the week ended Nov. 4, up from 429,000 over the week ended Oct. 7 and 271,000 over the one ended Sept. 30, Hangzhou-based DeepSeek said yesterday. Users consume around 92 trillion tokens a day.

The number of third-party plug-ins has surged to about 35,000 since DeepSeek Harness was released, and about 60 percent of users created or installed at least one third-party plugin. It is preparing a support program for plugin authors.

DeepSeek Harness is a software support framework built around large language models, designed to help AI agents manage and execute more complex tasks. It can be seen as a complete set of operating systems an LLM needs to truly become an agent.

As a benchmark for domestic LLMs, DeepSeek is accelerating evolution. On Oct. 31, DeepSeek Harness’ team published a technical article called ‘Exploring Super-Agent Design to a More Autonomous Agent System’ on its official WeChat account.

The article claims that improved model capabilities have given rise to new applications, and personal agents have begun to emerge rapidly. However, mainstream agent design still cannot support this mode at the multi-task and team-collaboration level, and the multi-task limit depends on people’s attention.

To overcome these limitations, it is necessary to break the binding between agents and a one-off manual session, making it a continuous entity that can maintain context across sessions and simultaneously advance multiple complex tasks without interfering with each other. DeepSeek refers to this form of agent and its system architecture as ‘super-agent.’

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: Chinese Robot Makers Boost Industrial Investment to Support Embodied AI Partners
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 13 -- Despite a cooling in embodied intelligence investment in the primary market, AgiBot, Unitree Robotics, and other leading Chinese robot manufacturers are ramping up industrial investment to drive growth across the industry and its supply chain by backing ecosystem partners.

AgiBot launched its Venture A Program for global early-stage entrepreneurs in August last year, aiming to incubate more than 50 projects in three years. The Shanghai-based company has since invested in more than 20 firms spanning sensors, chips, dexterous hands, biomimetic robots, data collection, and embodied artificial intelligence models.

AgiBot has expanded the program beyond the embodied intelligence supply chain to next-generation AI infrastructure, next-gen models, and the space, life sciences, and other areas. It also unveiled the "Yuansheng Fertile Soil Program," opening up its accumulated hardware platforms, application scenarios, and data capabilities to innovators across the industry.

Unitree recently teamed up with HongShan Capital Group to launch the Shanyu·Create Initiative, which will identify and invest in early-stage ventures in embodied intelligence, robot applications, critical upstream and downstream technologies, and other frontier hard-tech sectors. In addition, its earlier Yuchuang Program aims to incubate more than 200 ecosystem companies as a long-term strategic investment, with likely cooperation worth several billion yuan (hundreds of millions of US dollars) over the next five years.

Galaxea AI, an embodied intelligent robot developer, partnered with existing investor Cathay Capital to launch the Xingtu Program, planning to invest CNY1 billion (USD149.9 million) over the next five years to provide capital, technology, and industry resources to early-stage embodied intelligence startups.

Embodied intelligence remains in its early stages, and leading companies' investments in upstream and downstream players help strengthen supply chains and connect industry resources, while also serving as a strategic move for future competition, multiple industry insiders told Yicai. However, whether such investments can build a lasting competitive edge still depends on whether these industrial partnerships form healthy commercial relationships, they pointed out.

Embodied intelligence is still in its early stages, Cai Bingzhen, head of the High-Tech Robotics Industry Research Institute, said to Yicai, adding that supporting ecosystem partners helps advance the industry and its supply chain.

As the sector matures, ecosystem-building will become an important competitive strategy, according to a person who previously worked at an investment institution. Equity investment can be used to forge ties with dexterous hand makers, data analytics, and other key links, better serving a company's core business, the person pointed out.

A reasonable boundary must be maintained between investment and industrial cooperation, said Wang Han, a partner at Yaolin Capital. As the primary market cools and initial public offering reviews slow, some companies' pre-IPO shares have become cheaper, giving leading firms a price advantage when they invest, while also helping them build industrial partnerships, he stressed.

Some investments may be tied to product procurement commitments, Wang noted. Buying at market prices is a relatively healthy form of cooperation, but if a procurement amount is agreed before the investment, the deal is more likely aimed at using the investment to drive sales, he said.

Whether such investments can build an industry moat ultimately depends on whether a healthy supply-chain relationship can be established, Wang added.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: Lilly Wins China’s First Approval for Weight-Loss Pill
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 13 -- Eli Lilly’s Chinese arm said the US drugmaker’s weight-loss pill orforglipron, a small-molecule glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, has become the first GLP-1 oral drug to receive the green light for adult weight management in China.

The National Medical Products Administration approved orforglipron as a Class 1 new drug for weight management in obese and overweight adults with at least one weight-related comorbidity as an adjunct to diet and increased physical activity, Eli Lilly China announced yesterday. The company is also researching the pill to treat type 2 diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea, knee osteoarthritis pain, hypertension, peripheral arterial disease, and stress urinary incontinence, it added.

Orforglipron ’s indication for type 2 diabetes in adults is under review by the NMPA, Lilly pointed out.

Lilly’s top obesity drug tirzepatide generated more than USD43.7 billion in revenue in the first nine months of this year. But the injection’s accessibility is affected because some patients are afraid of needles and the need for refrigerated transport or storage. Orforglipron, which is taken once a day, addresses these pain points, according to the company.

In April, the US Food and Drug Administration approved orforglipron for weight loss in adults, making it the world’s first oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist. The drug has brought USD281 million in revenue since launching in the second quarter, including USD184 million last quarter, according to Lilly’s latest earnings report.

Danish pharmaceutical giant Novo Nordisk also has a GLP-1 weight-loss pill, the oral version of semaglutide. China has approved the drug for blood sugar control, while regulators accepted its application for long-term weight management in August.

On Nov. 9, the FDA said that using GLP-1 receptor agonists may increase the risk of a rare eye disease that can lead to permanent vision loss, requiring applicants for all related drugs to add a risk warning. According to the list, drugs with the warning include injectable semaglutide, liraglutide, and tirzepatide, as well as the semaglutide and orforglipron pills.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: Chinese Smart Glasses Market Is Still Chasing Breakthrough Moment Despite Rising Sales
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 13 -- China’s smart glasses sales have climbed during the Double 11 shopping festival this year. However, industry insiders warned that no widely accepted consumer application has emerged yet.

The value of smart glasses sales on JD.Com surged 150 percent during this year’s Double 11 shopping gala ended on Nov. 11 from a year earlier, with the value of display smart glasses sales up nearly fourfold, according to data from the Chinese e-commerce giant.

Online retail volume of smart glasses during the first three weeks of Double 11 reached 88,000 units, generating CNY160 million (USD23.8 million) in sales, according to data from market research firm AVC.

Smart glasses demand is concentrated at the two ends of the price spectrum, Li Xiaoxian, analyst at AVC, told Yicai. Cheaper products chase value and high-end products offer upgraded optical performance and office functions, while mid-range products suffer from vague positioning and underperform, he explained.

Display augmented reality glasses priced at around CNY1,000 (USD149) are the current market hotspot, a senior industry insider told Yicai. However, the broader sector remains unprofitable because of the fierce competition despite robust sales growth, they added.

During Double 11, RayNeo launched its 35-gram iO AR glasses, supporting translation, transcription, and navigation, priced at about CNY2,000, Coolpad Group partnered with JD.Com to release artificial intelligence camera glasses priced at around CNY500 (USD 74), and Inmo introduced a binocular full-color smart glasses model.

At the 2026 Baidu World Conference yesterday, Baidu previewed a 38-gram smart cloud AR glasses model co-developed with Antavic Technology, expected to hit the market next month, priced from CNY1,699. The product supports navigation, translation, teleprompter, and meeting transcription functions, Antavic’s Chief Executive Yan Pengfei told Yicai.

Antavic handles the hardware research, development, and manufacturing, while Baidu supplies the AI model and integrates the product into its ecosystem.

“While smart glasses were hot during Double 11, the long-anticipated breakthrough in the market has not arrived yet,” said Liu Chuang, researcher at Runto. He believes one reason is the mismatch between product offerings and users’ genuine, high-frequency needs.

Smart glasses have yet to form a widely accepted value proposition for the public, Liu noted, adding that the main reason is that existing products lack a killer use case ordinary consumers view as indispensable. The value they deliver is auxiliary rather than essential.

Liu believes smart glasses sales over the past two years were heavily tied to promotional campaigns, as organic consumer demand is limited and many orders stem from impulse purchases driven by promotions.

Most smart glasses sold in China target office scenarios, said Li. The sales growth mainly comes from this segment, whose growth potential is relatively limited, he pointed out.

Entertainment represents the biggest potential growth driver for smart glasses, Li believes. Even so, entertainment products remain in the trial stage, with limited supply, high prices, steep learning curves, and long cycles for building the content ecosystem, which will likely prevent rapid penetration in the near term.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Futura Costaglione

data.title: Double 11 Shopping Festival Ends With USD266 Billion in Sales Driven by Service Consumption
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 13 -- China’s Double 11 shopping festival has concluded, with e-commerce platforms racking up CNY1.776 trillion (USD266.3 billion) in sales, according to a report. Service consumption was a key driver, and hobby and pet products also posted strong growth.

Chinese e-commerce sites’ sales rose 4.8 percent this year’s Double 11 from a year earlier, according to a report released by Syntum yesterday. Service consumption grew at a faster pace than goods consumption, continuing an overall trend in the first three quarters, when online retail sales of services expanded 5.3 percent, and online retail sales of goods rose 3.8 percent from the same period last year.

More than 300 million service orders were placed on JD.Com during Double 11, per data released by the Chinese e-commerce giant. Sales of housekeeping cleaning packages jumped over 550 percent, pet de-shedding services surged 46-fold, range hood cleaning climbed more than 250 percent, and refrigerator cleaning grew nearly six-fold from a year earlier.

JD.Com’s moving service has expanded to 12 Chinese cities, with orders soaring nearly fourfold. Meanwhile, orders for its auto care services, door-to-door repair services for two-wheeled vehicles, and health services rose 167 percent, 140 percent, and 300 percent, respectively, in the period.

JoyExpress, JD.Com’s online retail business in Europe, launched Double 11 promotions for European consumers, with home appliance sales up more than ninefold, aided by related services.

A JoyExpress delivery rider in Germany said it delivered and installed products to five households on Nov. 10 alone. The ‘delivery plus installation’ service covers not only specialty categories, such as solar panels, lawn mowers, and pool-cleaning robots, but also delivery, installation, removal, and recycling of old large home appliances, such as televisions and washing machines.

Hobby-related spending was also hot this year. Sales of smart perler bead boards exceeded CNY5 million (USD749,600) during Double 11, according to Alibaba Group Holding’s e-commerce platform Taobao. One cosplay product sold more than 100,000 units. Pet owners stocked up on 43.6 million bags of cat food and 5.9 million bags of cat litter.

Consumers mostly adopted rational consumption behavior during Double 11, said Guo Tao, angel investor and veteran artificial intelligence expert. Impulsive purchases and blind stockpiling dropped noticeably, while price comparison and scrutiny of marketing gimmicks became common habits, he explained.

Price sensitivity in essential categories remained high, but weight in consumption decisions is shifting toward the overall experience, Guo noted. Consumers no longer focus only on headline discounts, as they also check delivery times, return and exchange terms, after-sales commitments, and supporting services, and prefer simple, transparent direct price cuts over complicated discount schemes.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: China's Changan Auto to Sell 10% Stake in EV Brand Avatr for at Least USD479.7 Million
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 13 -- Chinese state-owned carmaker Changan Automobile said it plans to sell a 10 percent stake in its electric vehicle brand Avatr Technology for a minimum of CNY3.2 billion (USD479.7 million), with the move coming while Avatr pushes ahead with its Hong Kong initial public offering amid slowing sales and shrinking cash reserves.

 

Changan plans to sell just over 306.5 million shares in Avatr, with the disclosure period running through Dec. 10, the Chongqing-based company announced yesterday on the Shanghai United Assets and Equity Exchange. Avatr has a valuation floor of CNY31.8 billion (USD4.8 billion), about in line with its post-money valuation after its Series C funding round in December 2024.

 

A buyer must pay a CNY500 million (USD75 million) deposit and settle the full purchase price in a lump sum within three working days of signing the equity transfer contract, Changan noted. It also must commit that its funding sources are lawful and compliant, that the deal will not affect Avatr's planned listing, and that it has no competing business with the brand.

 

Changan plans for the new investor to focus on supporting high-end brand channel building and overseas market expansion, it told Yicai. After the deal closes, the carmaker will continue backing Avatr in core areas including technology research and development, vehicle manufacturing, and the supply chain, it added.

 

Changan holds about 41 percent of Avatr, making it the largest shareholder, followed by battery giant Contemporary Amperex Technology with around 9.2 percent, meaning a potential single buyer of the 10 percent stake will become the brand's second-largest shareholder.

 

Avatr sold 20,160 vehicles from January through May this year, according to its prospectus. However, data from the China Passenger Car Association shows domestic retail sales dropped below 3,000 units last month.

 

In addition, Avatr's cash on hand fell to around CNY6.2 billion in late April this year from CNY9.7 billion on Dec. 31 and CNY19.3 billion at the end of 2024, making a drop of more than CNY800 million a month.

 

For yet-to-be-profitable automakers listed in Hong Kong, sales expectations affect revenue growth and the price-to-sales ratio, while cash reserves and the cash burn rate relate to a company's cash runway, a key metric watched by capital market investors, industry experts told Yicai.

 

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: Tech Boom Helps China’s Trade Jump 38% in October
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 12 -- China’s trade jumped again last month, buoyed partly by the technology sector, with momentum likely to moderate in the coming months as year-earlier comparative bases rise.

Imports and exports reached USD719.38 billion in October, up 38 percent from a year ago, with the highest import growth seen since May 2021, according to data released by the General Administration of Customs.

Exports jumped 35 percent to USD412.33 billion, compared with a 36 percent rise in September. Imports surged 42 percent to USD307.05 billion, versus a 31 percent increase the previous month. The trade surplus stood at USD105.28 billion.

In the first 10 months of this year, trade reached USD6.52 trillion, up 25 percent from the same period last year. Exports rose 23 percent to USD3.78 trillion, with the growth led by integrated circuits, automatic data processing equipment, and components related to artificial intelligence. Last month alone, exports of these products doubled year on year.

Imports from January to October amounted to USD2.74 trillion, up 29 percent.

Trade with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations totaled USD1.12 trillion in the 10 months, up 30 percent from a year ago, the GAC data showed. Trade with the European Union reached USD769.37 billion, up 13 percent, and with the United States it was USD522.7 billion, up 11 percent.

In the same period, imports and exports between China and countries co-developing the Belt and Road Initiative jumped 24 percent to USD3.33 trillion.

Exports of AI-related products remain robust, but year-on-year growth in export prices may have peaked, China International Capital Corporation said in a research report. In terms of imports, the Middle East conflict drove up energy prices, and the increase in energy imports was the main contributor to the increase in October.

Looking at the last two months of the year, growth in AI-related exports may slow as the comparative bases from a year earlier rise alongside a potential cooling of AI investment in the United States. The China-US trade truce is also now set to expire in January.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: China's Non-Bank Financial Institution Deposits Reach 11.2% of Total Deposits at End of Third Quarter
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 12 -- Deposits held by non-bank financial institutions in China accounted for 11.2 percent of all deposits as of Sept. 30, up from 9 percent at the end of 2023, according to a report released by the People’s Bank of China yesterday.

The increase reflects changes in the country's financing structure, growing public financial awareness and interest in wealth management, as well as differences in returns across financial products, the report said. Deposits held by non-bank financial institutions surged 19.1 percent at the end of the third quarter from a year earlier.

The growing preference among households and businesses for time deposits over demand deposits is also worth noting. The share of corporate demand deposits tumbled to 27.9 percent at the end of the third quarter from 38.4 percent at the end of 2020, the central bank said. The share of household demand deposits dropped to 25.4 percent from 35.3 percent over the same period.

By contrast, in economies such as the United States and Europe, deposits serve primarily as transactional funds, resulting in a higher proportion of demand deposits, industry experts said. In China, time deposits account for a larger proportion, largely because bank deposits make up the bulk of household financial assets. In a low-interest-rate environment, Chinese households are more inclined to place their money in time deposits to earn higher returns.

In terms of deposit holders, corporate deposits in China stood at about CNY172 trillion (USD25.8 trillion) as of Sept. 30, accounting for 49.3 percent of all deposits. This was higher than the corresponding share of 35.6 percent in the US and 40.2 percent in Japan, largely due to deposits held by government agencies, public institutions and non-bank financial institutions.

The changes also reflect the growing diversion of household and corporate savings into financial products such as stocks, bonds, wealth management products and asset management products, with funds subsequently flowing back into the banking system in the form of deposits held by non-bank financial institutions, financial experts said.

At the same time, the relatively high proportion of time deposits held by businesses, government agencies, public institutions and non-bank financial institutions also provides some insight into the investment and consumption appetite of companies and households.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: China's State-Owned Broadcasters Turn to AI Dramas as Short Videos Squeeze Traditional TV
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 12 -- China's state-owned broadcasters are ramping up production of artificial intelligence-generated dramas and building dedicated content platforms as they seek to counter growing competition from mobile short-video services.

Mango Excellent Media, Wasu Media Network and Hicon Network Technology are among the companies developing AI-powered platforms to automate content creation, Yicai learned.

The push into AI dramas marks a shift in broadcasters' business strategies, but profitability remains uncertain as revenue-sharing mechanisms and consumer payment models are still evolving.

Broadcasters Build AI Production Capabilities

Several broadcasters have already begun putting these plans into action. Hunan province-based entertainment company Mango established an AI-generated content innovation center this year and launched a dedicated AIGC channel on its Mango TV streaming platform.

Mango's Journey to the West: The Sequel, an AI-generated fantasy drama inspired by the Chinese literary classic Journey to the West, became China's first AI-generated long-form series to air on a television station. It has also attracted advertisers, including title sponsors.

Hangzhou-headquartered cable television and digital media operator Wasu has developed an AIGC platform called Shihua that streamlines short-drama production from scriptwriting to regulatory review, enabling mass production of AI-generated dramas featuring lifelike human characters, animated comic dramas and other animations.

Jinan-based digital media services provider Hicon has developed an AI platform that automates film and television production from concept to finished product. It has also begun collaborating with Chinese technology giant ByteDance's short-drama app Hongguo and short-video platform Douyin on AI-generated animated comic dramas.

AI is changing not just how broadcasters produce content but also how they organize their businesses. AI has evolved from a cost-cutting tool into a technology reshaping film and TV production, Dong Min, secretary-general of the China Video Industry Association, told Yicai.

Broadcaster-backed companies are rapidly expanding into AI short dramas by leveraging their existing TV distribution networks, Dong said. Many have elevated their AI content divisions to the same organizational level as traditional program production centers and have begun airing AI dramas on satellite TV channels.

A senior executive at a broadcasting company told Yicai that producing AI dramas is part of the industry's efforts to adapt to the pressure from mobile short-video services.

Broadcasters have technical and creative strengths in short-drama production, the insider said, adding that the AI specialists they attract can compete with those working for online video and short-drama platforms.

New Revenue Models Take Shape

Beyond changing production, AI short dramas are opening up new ways for broadcasters to make money, the above-mentioned executive said.

Unlike traditional films and TV series, which rely mainly on advertising and sponsorships, short dramas can generate additional revenue through on-demand viewing fees and sales of products featured in or promoted alongside the shows, models that consumers are increasingly embracing.

A new distribution platform demonstrates those opportunities. The Audiovisual Content Center of China's National Radio and Television Administration recently launched a video app called Juhaokan, offering an integrated channel for distributing dramas and sharing revenue.

Going forward, broadcasters could earn additional income by distributing their AI dramas beyond their own channels, the executive suggested.

Despite progress in production and distribution, turning AI dramas into a sustainable business will depend on mature revenue-sharing mechanisms, clear regulatory standards and households' willingness to pay for content on TV screens.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Emmi Laine

data.title: [Fact Check] Tencent Has No Plans to Cut 50% of Workforce, Eyes Faster Organizational Reforms, Sources Say
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 12 -- Online claims that Tencent Holdings is preparing to lay off half of its employees are untrue, Yicai learned from people familiar with the matter. Rather, the Chinese internet behemoth’s management signaled the need to accelerate organizational reforms during a livestream yesterday, they said.

Management used the livestream to signal plans to streamline organizational hierarchies and strengthen talent management, the sources said. Executives noted that some middle managers were reluctant to take action, while front-line employees were highly motivated. They also stressed the need to maintain a sense of urgency and proactively embrace change in the artificial intelligence era. Tencent Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Pony Ma reportedly adopted quite a stern tone during the discussion.

The online rumors also claimed that Tencent management said during the livestream that “it is already a matter of survival,” and that the Shenzhen-based firm had “previously been too lenient with employees,” “not set high-enough standards” and that “senior staff should make way for younger colleagues with relevant expertise and give them more authority.”

Tencent management specifically emphasized that the latest initiative is different from the cost-cutting and efficiency drive launched a few years ago, the sources said. The previous campaign was relatively reactive and focused more on reducing costs. This time, however, Tencent is proactively positioning itself for the AI era with a greater emphasis on improving efficiency and productivity. The goal is to unleash teams’ ability to create new value, empower front-line employees to take the initiative, and make middle management flatter and more agile.

Tencent’s management also said that, to adapt to the changes ahead, Tencent needs to proactively explore new approaches and business opportunities. Half of the workforce should focus on improving efficiency in existing core businesses, while the other half should explore AI-native approaches and identify new areas for growth. This represents a reallocation of the company’s resources to adapt to the AI era.

In fact, Tencent management had already signaled earlier that it would change its business model in the AI era, with organizational streamlining being a key priority.

In an interview with Yicai and other media outlets in June, Dowson Tong, Tencent’s senior executive vice president and CEO of its Cloud and Smart Industries Group, said that teams developing AI-native product R&D teams have become flatter than before and will continue to shrink in size, with development increasingly carried out by small teams of three to five people.

Liu Yi, head of Tencent’s CodeBuddy and WorkBuddy products, also said in the interview that within his team the only organizational units are groups, with no additional management layers. Such a flat organizational structure helps eliminate inefficiencies and information distortion caused by reporting requirements and organizational barriers between employees and management levels, he added.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: China’s Cosco Shipping Energy to Expand Fleet With 40 VLCCs by 2030
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 12 -- Cosco Shipping Energy Transportation plans to expand its fleet of very large crude carriers by 40 vessels over the next four years amid an aging global VLCC fleet, tight medium- to long-term oil tanker capacity, and a buoyant deep-sea shipping market.

The China Cosco Shipping subsidiary will add 10 green energy powered VLCCs by the end of 2030 at a cost of CNY9.5 billion (USD1.4 billion), according to announcements made this week.

Six will be built by affiliate Cosco Shipping Heavy Industry for CNY5.7 billion (tax included), and the rest by China State Shipbuilding’s Dalian shipyard for CNY3.8 billion (tax included). Deliveries are scheduled for between the second half of 2029 and the end of 2030, and payment will be in Chinese yuan.

Cosco Shipping Energy will charter the other 30 VLCCs. Fourteen will be newbuilds owned by six bank-affiliated financial leasing companies, including 10 powered by green energy and the rest using conventional propulsion. The 20-year rental cost for the 14 should be no more than CNY17.4 billion (USD2.6 billion), the Shanghai-based company said.

The remaining 16 vessels will be newbuilds chartered from Cosco Shipping Energy’s affiliate Cosco Shipping Development. Powered by green methanol or liquefied natural gas, they will be built by China State Shipbuilding’s Dalian yard. No costs were disclosed for these.

By adding scarce VLCC capacity, expanding its fleet, and improving its structure, Cosco Shipping Energy will enhance its service capability and market share in the crude oil deep-sea shipping market, the company pointed out. In addition, this will help strengthen profitability and align with the global shipping industry’s decarbonization drive.

After rising by as much as 2.3 percent earlier today, Cosco Shipping Energy [SHA: 600026] closed 1.5 percent lower at CNY16.71 (USD2.51) per share. Cosco Shipping Development [SHA: 601866] lost 0.8 percent to CNY2.35 (35 US cents), while China State Shipbuilding gave up 0.4 percent to CNY34.20. The broader Shanghai market dropped 0.7 percent.

Cosco Shipping Development is the industrial-financial platform of Shipping giant Cosco Shipping Group. Cosco Shipping Energy is an ocean-going energy transportation services provider under the group, while Cosco Shipping Heavy Industry is the shipbuilding arm of Cosco Shipping Group.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Martin Kadiev

data.title: Baidu’s New LLM Trading Platform Exceeds 50 Million Average Daily Calls in First Month
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 12 -- Chinese internet giant Baidu has officially launched its large language model trading platform Ciyuansuo at the 2026 Baidu World Conference, aiming to address the issues of a mixed-quality model market and users’ lack of trust when choosing models.

Ciyuansuo has been operating for one month, Baidu’s founder Robin Li said at the conference today. More than 100 resource providers have already joined Ciyuansuo, which has reached 50 million average daily application programming interface calls and 700 billion average daily used tokens, he added.

“Ciyuansuo is an exchange for LLMs, enabling enterprises and even individuals to easily find, purchase, and use trustworthy model tokens,” Li explained.

In the first three quarters of the year, a new model was released almost every day, sometimes even multiple ones in a day, Li noted, adding that the surge in model supply did not translate into better user experience. “After all the picking and choosing, people still don’t feel confident or dare to use them.”

In other words, the LLM market lacked an infrastructure that could serve as a ‘credit intermediary,’ and that is exactly where the value of an exchange lies. According to information disclosed at the conference, Ciyuansuo focuses on two core capabilities: authenticity verification and credit assessment.

The authenticity verification function uses technical methods, such as model fingerprint matching, capability testing, and performance and availability checks, to validate model resources.

Meanwhile, the credit assessment function establishes a credit rating for model providers through regular spot checks, dial tests, and full-chain, real-time call monitoring, offering customers neutral, credible, and transparent model trading services.

This means LLM providers now have something akin to a “credit record” in the trading process, and buyers can make decisions based on publicly transparent ratings.

As competition in the artificial intelligence industry intensifies, securing a place in the model trading market may hold more potential than simply releasing another LLM. After all, an exchange's value has never depended on the traded assets.

Baidu also unveiled other achievements at the conference. In foundational models, the company released Ernie 5.5 Flash Preview, and in application models, it launched the Ernie Lightning deep thinking model and the Ernie-Wizshot-Me, which were simultaneously deployed on Baidu Intelligent Cloud's Qianfan LLM Platform, opening API services to enterprise customers and partners.

Moreover, digital-human agent Baidu Yijing introduced Short Comic Drama Studio at the conference, covering an end-to-end creation workflow from concept and script-writing to storyboarding and final production.

On Baidu Yijing, creators can localize verified works by adapting plots, characters, and scenes for overseas markets in one click, helping short comic dramas go global. Based on Baidu’s self-developed video generation model, it costs only 20 Chinese cents (3 US Cents) per second.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: Growing AI Use Marks This Year's Double 11 Shopping Gala But Human Touch Remains Crucial
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 12 -- With artificial intelligence deeply embedded in this year's Double 11, helping vendors streamline their operations and making shopping more convenient for consumers, humans still remain in control during the online retail festival in China, according to industry insiders.

The use of AI use in Double 11 is not fragmented as in previous years, Guo Tao, an angel investor and veteran AI expert, told Yicai. Major e-commerce platforms have put AI shop assistants in key roles on their sites and enabled data interoperability across large language models, product information, and promotional offers, allowing AI to make recommendations based on user preferences and calculate the best discounts, Guo noted.

Many vendors have also incorporated AI tools into their operations, Guo noted. “AI is no longer simply helping merchants cut costs, but it also contributes to identifying user needs and driving transaction conversions," Guo said. "The integration of tech, data, and business workflows has lifted the overall application density of AI."

AI has become a core operating system for Yaowang Technology, said Shao Qin, vice president of the Shenzhen-listed livestream sales and digital marketing services provider. From pre-broadcast preparation to post-broadcast review, AI has shortened the workflow and boosted efficiency, Shao noted.

For example, AI cut the time needed for product selection, quality control, and content planning from seven days to just one to two days, while analysis of broadcast outcomes, previously based solely on human judgment and experience, is now AI-powered and multidimensional, Shao said.

A notable shift for Qianxun during this year's Double 11 operations was that AI evolved from an auxiliary tool used sporadically into a routine element, according to a senior executive at the multi-channel network agency. AI has entered more livestream sales segments, benefiting hosts, customer service teams, and supply-chain teams, the person said.

“Our principle is clear,” he stressed. “We delegate foundational, repetitive, and high-volume tasks to AI, while leaving final judgment and accountability for outcomes to our human staff.”

Customer service is where AI delivers the most surprising results, the executive said, pointing out that Double 11 brings exception number of user inquiries. Staff previously spent long hours cross-checking information, but with the help of AI, work that once took at least two hours can be done in about 10 minutes, he said.

Consumers are also taking full advantage of AI tools. According to a report by Analysys, they have been using the technology to compare prices, verify promotional terms, and compare product specifications, helping them to navigate the overwhelming amount of information from countless vendors during Double 11. In this way, AI has reduced both the time and risk involved in purchase decisions.

Zhuanzhuan, a second-hand trading platform, has rolled out an AI assistant to help consumers assess the condition of used mobile phones and luxury bags, a representative told Yicai, adding that it shifts the process from subjective assessment to objective, data-driven judgment.

"We apply a consistent standard for AI scoring of items,” the person said. The results are replicable, traceable, and scalable."

More than 60 percent of Double 11 shoppers are willing to try AI tools for price comparison and product filtering, Guo pointed out, citing industry research. However, few are comfortable letting AI place orders autonomously, with most regarding it as a helper rather than a decision-maker, AI expert Guo Tao said.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Martin Kadiev

data.title: China's Inbound Tourism Revenue to Hit USD470 Billion, Make Up 1.5% of GDP by 2040, UBS Predicts
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 12 -- China's revenue from inbound tourism could reach USD470 billion by 2040, accounting for 1.5 percent of the country’s gross domestic product, according to the head of China leisure and transportation research at UBS Securities.

As international flight networks expand, visa-free policies are further eased, and overseas visitors show growing interest in traveling and spending in China, inbound tourism is expected to become a key driver of China's services consumption growth, Chen Xin said at a media briefing on Nov. 10.

China's inbound tourism is expected to grow by more than 20 percent next year, he noted, adding that the growth mainly comes from three factors, along with favorable visa policies, more convenient payment options, and other services.

First, China is one of the safest countries in the world, drawing more and more overseas tourists and business travelers to return, bringing friends and family. Second, Chinese airlines have been steadily adding international routes, improving air connectivity with global markets. Third, Chinese airfares are more competitive than those of their overseas peers, partly because they can fly in Russian airspace.

The expansion of the aviation network is also helping China become an international transit hub. For instance, the share of international transit passengers at Shanghai’s two airports rose to 35 percent this year, up from 10 percent in 2024.

Chinese carriers have added multiple European routes and expanded into markets such as Canada this year, Chen said. As international flight volumes continue to increase, China is expected to further strengthen its position as a hub in the global aviation network.

In terms of consumption, inbound tourists are contributing not only through passenger traffic but also through spending on shopping, hotels, and other services. Their per-capita spending is about USD800, according to data disclosed by Chen.

Moreover, as more and more foreign visitors extend their trips from first-tier cities, such as Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou, to smaller cities like Hangzhou, Nanjing, and Suzhou, in-depth tourism is expected to drive travel and consumption demand in more destinations.

China's manufacturing sector offers a wide range of products at competitive prices, with similar goods at airports and other retail channels typically priced 20 to 30 percent lower than overseas, giving overseas visitors more shopping options, Chen said.

Sustaining long-term inbound tourism growth will require continued supply-side improvements, including adding more international destinations and flights, expanding high-end hotel supply in different cities, and improving the convenience of visa, payment, and transportation services, Chen suggested. Over the next few years, the expansion of international flight networks and overseas travelers’ spending will be key indicators for China's inbound tourism growth.

Editor: Futura Costaglione
